mechanism_claims.claim: Pénaud's hélicoptère is powered by twisted rubber (a rubber band wound up, then released).
citations: Commons File:Penaud's Helicopter.jpg (PD), description: "Adolphe Pénaud's rubber band driven helicopter model, featuring contra-rotating propellers, 1872." https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Penaud%27s_Helicopter.jpg

Commons File:1900 Wright Glider (reproduction) - DPLA - c3b0fb1f8a58d97ba49af5638476a035 (page 2).jpg (CC0, NASM text): "In 1878 their father gave them a toy flying helicopter model powered by strands of twisted rubber." (a Pénaud-type toy; supports 'twisted rubber')
mechanism_claims.used_in: BB-02/03 winding, release, band snap (snap itself is fiction)

mechanism_claims.claim: The hélicoptère has two rotors on one shaft that turn in opposite directions.
citations: Commons File:Penaud's Helicopter.jpg description: "featuring contra-rotating propellers"
Plate PENAUD-PLATE (top figure) shows two rotors on one shaft.

mechanism_claims.claim: The Lilienthal apparatus is a hang glider, controlled by the pilot shifting his body weight (hanging by the arms, legs free).
citations: Commons File:1895 Lilienthal Normal-Segelapparat (1928 replica) at Musée de l'air et de l'espace, Le Bourget, France (53367634045).jpg, description by Alan Wilson (CC BY-SA 2.0; cited as text only, image not used): "Control was achieved by the pilot shifting his own weight in the glider."

LoC https://www.loc.gov/item/2001699884/ 'O. Lilienthal - flying machine Patented Aug. 20, 1895' (design drawing for a glider invented and patented by Otto Lilienthal) - identifies the apparatus as a glider; does not by itself state weight-shift.
Engravings PSM V46 D647/D648 show the pilot hanging between the wings with legs free.
mechanism_claims.used_in: BB-07 run and lift-off; BB-08 legs swing forward on the hip pin

mechanism_claims.claim: Raising the nose (a higher angle of attack) costs forward speed, and past a critical angle the wing stalls: lift breaks down.
citations: US Federal Aviation Administration, Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25), ch. 5 'Aerodynamics of Flight', sections on angle of attack and stalls; a US government work (public domain, 17 U.S.C. 105). Paraphrased, not quoted; the handbook was not fetched in this session (Commons API returned 'too many requests' on 2026-11-16), so the citation is from the published text, not a downloaded copy.
mechanism_claims.confidence: documented (general aerodynamics; citation not re-read this session)
mechanism_claims.used_in: BB-08: nose rises 5 -> 35 deg, x-advance decays (exposure.json); header 'le décrochage'; the 'monter' -> 's'arrêter' correction

mechanism_claims.claim: The glider comes to a complete stop in the air, hangs still f540-554, then slides back tail first.
mechanism_claims.used_in: BB-08 hang and slide, BB-09 slide into the crash; declared under fiction A3

mechanism_claims.claim: (not used on screen) Lilienthal died after a gliding accident, 1896.
citations: Same Le Bourget description; NASM text in Wright glider record.
mechanism_claims.used_in: NOT used: the film names no historical person; recorded only so nobody adds it.

fictions.name: paper wing
fictions.machine: handmade (ribbed cream paper piece with pen ribs; no historical source)
fictions.note: Wholly invented attempt; the paper folds back and he sits down.

fictions.name: rotor use
fictions.note: The machine is real (a model about the size of a hand); a man lifting with it, the rise of ~1 panel-height, and the band snap are fiction.

fictions.name: glide
fictions.note: The apparatus is real; this flight is fiction: the stall at f528 (its cause is cited in EV-NOSEHIGH-SLOW-a), the full stop and still hang f540-554 and the tail-first slide (EV-NOSEHIGH-SLOW-b) and the crash at f605.

fictions.name: Monsieur Pique-Vent
fictions.machine: puppet cut from the PSM pilot figure
fictions.note: A fictional inventor operating real engraved machines. No slip names Lilienthal or Pénaud. Declared on screen (repair 1): graphite line under the title of both planches, 'M. Pique-Vent, inventeur inventé - vols imaginés', readable in the wide shots f0-24, f384-432, f684-720.

handmade.made: 20.0 s air bed assembled by crossfading (0.4 s equal-power) shuffled and partly reversed slices of MIA-AIR-A and MIA-AIR-B, loudness-matched, 0.5 s fades; mono 48 kHz, about -42 dBFS RMS. Spectrogram checked: no speech.
greyscale crops for GrabCut (unit 2); not yet cut
check only: crops remapped to warm ink (45,38,32) on page cream (242,228,212) to confirm the engraving reads on the page

absences: Standalone PD magpie wood engraving (Brehms "Elster" single figure, Bewick History of British Birds woodcut): not found by Commons search ("Thomas Bewick magpie" query hit API 429; "Elster Holzstich", "Mützel Elster", "magpie flying illustration 19th" returned nothing usable). The Brehms 1893 "Raben" plate magpie is used instead (partly occluded).
A magpie engraving in FLIGHT: none found. Flying pose is built from the Brehms body + the Penny Magazine 1837 spread-wing woodcut.
John Bewick, "A Magpie" (Yale Center for British Art, CC0): a magpie, but watercolour with blue-green tint, not line; downloaded for review, rejected for the two-value page.

Die Gartenlaube (1887) b 698 (PD) and Meyer, Zeit-Vertreib 1752 Tafel 100 (PD): candidate magpie plates, not downloaded (upload.wikimedia.org 429 robot-policy for the rest of the session); unseen, so not assessed.
Naumann 1901 "Elster und Dohle" (PD): colour lithograph, perched; not used (as in the test shot).

Clean long outdoor air in the Moving Image Archive cache: scanned all ~250 clips with audio for speech-free stretches; the longest outdoor ones are only 1.6-2.4 s (refuge films are narrated throughout, others scored). Hence the assembled 20 s bed from two short spans. 7ad22207, 3b4530d3 (rest), 965fd226 (music), 74442368 (narration), a8cb43a2 (no audio track) rejected.
Archive rights pages (movingimagearchive.com) unreachable (proxy 403): rights taken from the local cache metadata instead.
Nose-high stall citation: cited from the FAA handbook text (US government work) without a fetched copy; Commons search rate-limited on 2026-11-16.
